title: Hagelloch 1861, its periods from CDC's Pink Book

source.citation: CDC. Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (the Pink Book), chapter 13: Measles. Page dated 24 April 2024.

evidence.quote: The time from exposure to rash onset averages 14 days
evidence.working: 14 days from exposure to the rash, less the 4 days a person transmits before it: 10 days infected and not yet infectious, on average. The chapter gives averages only; no spread is assumed here, so every child takes 10.

source.citation: CDC. Epidemiology and Prevention of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (the Pink Book), chapter 13: Measles. Page dated 24 April 2024.

evidence.quote: transmissible from 4 days before through 4 days after rash onset
evidence.working: 4 days before the rash, the day of the rash, and 4 days after: 9 days.

evidence.note: The spike's assumption; to be fitted to the 1861 curve. The chapter's secondary attack rate of more than 90% among susceptible close contacts would need at least 0.23 a day over 9 days; a Hagelloch household is not the same setting.
